settings.llm_hint: The scanner finds lines that look like a rate limit or provider error. With the check LLM on, it receives the last terminal lines and decides in a structured way whether the agent is really blocked (immediately red) or whether it was a menu line/retry (no incident). Off: hits turn yellow and become red after repetition or 5 min of silence. Applies to all agents. At most one request per run and 10 minutes.

ca.title: Coding agents
ca.intro: Which coding agent CLIs may this hub drive, and which model providers may each of them use? Forms only offer what is configured and enabled here.
ca.all_configured: All available coding agents are already configured.
ca.detect_note: Detection: for each known coding agent the hub checks whether its CLI is installed on this machine (command -v). New coding agents are added as plugins — see docs/plugins.md.
ca.providers_hint: Only selected providers appear in the forms — and of those only the ones with credentials (or key-free access).
ca.no_providers: subscription-based — the models come from the account, there is no provider selection
ca.delete_confirm: Really remove the coding agent „{label}“? Existing agents and runs keep their data.
form.branch_missing: Branch pattern is missing (expectation is not „none“).
run.branch_in_use: Branch „{branch}“ is already checked out in {worktree} — git grants a branch to only one worktree. Pick a branch that is free, or the expectation „new branch“ / „none“.
form.subscription_no_provider: {harness} runs on its subscription — there is no provider selection, only the model.
form.provider_unavailable: Provider „{provider}“ is not available for {harness} here (missing key or not enabled?). Possible: {list}
form.effort_invalid: Reasoning effort „{effort}“ is not possible for {target} — possible: {list}
effort.claude_cli: levels according to claude --help; applies to all subscription models
effort.cursor_in_id: cursor encodes the reasoning effort into the model ID (e.g. …-low, …-high, …-xhigh, …-max) — the level is already part of the model choice
effort.registry_only: levels according to the model catalog — opencode only accepts these
effort.none_in_catalog: the catalog lists no effort levels for this model
effort.intersection: levels known to BOTH hermes and the model
effort.no_common: hermes and the model have no common level
effort.model_unknown: no effort levels known for this model
sched.kind_weekly: on weekdays at a fixed time
sched.once_hint: Runs exactly once and resets itself to „manual“ afterwards. If the hub was off at the date, the start is caught up.
sched.cron_hint: Five fields: minute hour day month weekday.
sched.err_days: Please select at least one weekday.
sched.err_time: Time is missing or invalid (format HH:MM).
sched.err_anchor: A multi-week interval needs an anchor week.
sched.err_cron: „{expr}“ is not a 5-field cron (minute hour day month weekday), e.g. „0 6 * * 1-5“.
model.model_ph: Type a slug or pick from the list
or.hint: Without the checkbox OpenRouter decides itself. Only possible for opencode — hermes has no per-run argument for this.

tg.step2_hint: Send your bot a message in Telegram (e.g. /start) and then click:
tg.step3_hint: Then you are done — notifications go out for: done / failed / help call / anomaly / start deferred / quota ≥ 80 %. Every message has an „Open detail page“ button.
tg.no_chats: No messages found. Write to the bot first (/start), then click again.
tg.token_invalid: This does not look like a BotFather token.

js.no_creds: no providers available for this coding agent — type the model freely

js.stale: (list currently unreachable, showing the last state)

js.cursor_note: The reasoning effort is part of the ID (…-low/-medium/-high/-xhigh/-max); IDs ending in „-fast“ are cursor's fast mode — the default is the variant without.
js.type_filter: Typing filters; a custom slug is always allowed.
js.no_endpoints: — no data, type the slug below —
js.no_session: No tmux session anymore — the history is in the log below.
flows.intro: Flows react to finished runs (or a schedule) with no-code building blocks: message running agents, extract structured data from a report, start follow-up agents, notify via Telegram.
flows.name: Name
flows.delete_confirm: Delete this flow? Its past flow runs stay in the history.
flows.trigger.manual_hint: Only via "run now" — optionally with a finished run as the simulated trigger.
flows.trigger.repo_hint: Every run in this repo — from any of its agents and from single runs.
flows.trigger.flow_started: also runs started by a flow
flows.trigger.flow_started_hint: Off by default — loop guard: a flow that starts an agent would otherwise trigger itself again when that run ends. Use "wait" on the start step instead.
flows.runs.title: Flow runs
flows.editor.name_taken: A flow with this name already exists.
flows.editor.cron_invalid: The cron expression is not valid (5 fields).
flows.editor.variables_hint: Use {{…}} in any text field. Click to copy. Objects render as JSON; missing values as empty text. {{x | default: text}} sets a fallback.
flows.editor.sim_none: run now without a trigger run
flows.editor.run_unsaved: There are unsaved changes — run the saved version anyway?
flows.step.send_message.desc: Types a message into the tmux session of running runs (e.g. "main has moved, please pull").
flows.step.start_agent.desc: Starts a configured agent, optionally with extra prompt text. With "wait" the flow pauses until that run ends and stores its result.
flows.step.start_single_run.desc: Starts an ad-hoc run with its own prompt (as in the single-run form). With "wait" the flow pauses until it ends.
flows.step.kill_run.desc: Kills the tmux session of the selected running runs and marks them aborted.
flows.step.extract.desc: An LLM (OpenRouter, check-LLM settings) reads the report and/or terminal log of a run and fills the fields you define.
flows.step.set_var.desc: Stores a value under vars.<name>. A single {{path}} keeps its type, anything else becomes text.
flows.step.http_request.desc: Calls a webhook/API. The response (status, body, json) is stored in the output variable.
flows.step.condition.desc: Compares two values and continues in the true or false branch.
flows.step.switch_outcome.desc: Branches on done / failed / aborted (by default the trigger run's outcome).
flows.step.for_each.desc: Repeats the steps inside it once per element of a list — e.g. the open points from an extraction.
flows.step.delay.desc: Pauses the flow for the given minutes (survives a hub restart).
flows.step.telegram.desc: Sends a message over the configured Telegram bot, optionally with an attachment (e.g. the report).
flows.step.note.desc: Writes a line into the flow run log — handy for checking variables.
flows.field.wait: wait until the run ends (result → output variable)
flows.field.sourceRun.hint: Run ID or template; default: the trigger run.
flows.field.list.hint: Template yielding a list ({{vars.extracted.open_points}}); plain text is split line by line.
flows.field.itemVar.hint: The current element is vars.<name>, its position vars.<name>_index.
flows.editor.var_conditional: set inside a branch or loop — may be missing here
flows.editor.value_none: This operator compares nothing — no value needed.
flows.trigger.cron_no_run: A schedule has no trigger run: {{trigger.run.…}} stays empty, and steps that need a run outcome are only valid after a start step with "wait".
flows.warn.bool_value: {path} is a yes/no value — only "true" or "false" can ever match
flows.warn.number_value: {path} is a number — this value is not one
flows.warn.op_type: This operator cannot answer anything about {path} ({type})
flows.warn.needs_run_maybe: needs a finished run — a manual flow only has one when "run now" is given one
flows.placement.needs_run.rule: Needs a finished run: either from the trigger ("run finished") or from an earlier "Start agent" / "Start single run" with "wait".
flows.placement.needs_run.why: "{step}" cannot sit here: no finished run is available at this point, so the step could only ever take its fallback branch. Put it after a start step with "wait", or give the flow a "run finished" trigger.
flows.placement.needs_run_maybe.why: "{step}" only has a run when "run now" is given one — otherwise it falls through to its fallback.
flows.placement.after_stop.why: Nothing can follow "Stop" — the flow run has already ended there.
flows.placement.needs_run_target.rule: Only the target "the trigger run" needs a finished run. Every other target — an agent, a repo, all running runs, a run ID — reaches runs that have nothing to do with this flow and works in any flow.
flows.placement.needs_run_target.why: "{step}" is aimed at the trigger run, but there is none here. Pick another target — an agent, a repo or all running runs also reach agents outside this flow — or give the flow a "run finished" trigger.
flows.placement.needs_run_target_maybe.w: "{step}" is aimed at the trigger run, which a manual flow only has when "run now" is given one. Any other target works regardless.
flows.warn.needs_run_target_maybe: aimed at the trigger run — a manual flow only has one when "run now" is given one
